findings.reason: The protected Python solution places boxes into a warehouse entering from the left entrance. It replaces each room height with its prefix minimum (reachable clearance), sorts box heights in ascending order, and iterates through rooms from deepest to shallowest, matching the smallest unplaced box to each room if it fits. The solution runs in O(B log B + W) time and O(B + W) space; no candidate is required.

Prefix minimum clearance accurately reflects the max box height that can pass through all preceding rooms. Reversing clearance to process deepest rooms first combined with sorted boxes guarantees greedy small-to-small placement.

Sorting B boxes takes O(B log B) time. Computing W prefix minima and matching takes O(W) time. Total time is O(B log B + W) with O(B + W) auxiliary space for sorted boxes and clearance array. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts boxes and warehouse lists, returning the max integer number of boxes placed.

The approach accurately details prefix minimum clearance calculation, deepest-to-shallowest room iteration, greedy ascending box matching, and O(B log B + W) time / O(B + W) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover sorting effective capacities redundant overhead, repeated insertion simulation quadratic costs, heap selection complexity, tall rooms behind bottlenecks, smallest box fit failures, box/room count imbalances, and duplicate height handling.
